**Great lakes from a real place are water all over.** Relief of a real place left most of a large lake dry, with water only in odd rectangles and pieces cut along straight lines: around the Straits of Mackinac, with the real height at the sea level set to the lakes' 176 m, Lakes Michigan and Huron came out as green land. The elevation data gives such a lake's surface in rectangles of its sources, each flat at a level of its own a little apart, and each was taken for a terrace rather than a lake. Those rectangles now make one lake, at one level, its floor dug under it and its water reaching its shore, in a new world as over an existing map; and a wide flat at the real height you put at the sea level is water, even where it meets the lake's charted depths or the edge of the area. Many more small inland lakes come out as water too, and a lake's water no longer stands a block over its shore.
